verdict.rationale: Running a desktop OS on low-cost single-board computers is a fair question for an operating system, so the axis applies. However, the evidence pack never mentions single-board computers, ARM boards, or low-cost hardware support. The hardware it does reference is 2-in-1s, laptops, gaming PCs, and high-performance power-user machines, so there is no evidence Windows delivers a desktop developer experience on SBCs.
